subject: HelioSync Dedicated Commit: TPS tail modeling & throttling strategy
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Aditi Rao <aditi@heliosync.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: HelioSync dedicated commit — initial ask and data request

Hi Aditi,

Great to meet yesterday. As promised, I'm starting the thread to capture the committed capacity sizing conversation for HelioSync's planned Dedicated deployment. To size GPU pools and map SLO fit, we'll need a short traffic snapshot plus answers to a couple of quick questions below. If easier, attach a CSV with a 7-day sample and we can ingest it into our sizing worksheet.

What we need from you:
- Typical request distribution (percentage of short generation <128 tokens, 128-512, 512-2048, >2048)
- Peak concurrent requests (RPS) and any daily/weekly peak windows you expect
- Target p95 latency SLO (for user-facing flows) and p99 if you have it
- Percent of requests that use streaming or function-calls (affects concurrency/KV cache)
- Any blackout periods / quiet hours where you expect near-zero traffic

If you can share the token-profile CSV, we'll run three scenarios: conservative (95th tail headroom), recommended (80th with modest buffer), and cost-optimized (targeted quantization + batching). I'll loop Karthik and Priyom on the sizing math and a GPU tiling recommendation.

Next steps: please drop the CSV here or send to this thread and we'll aim to return a draft capacity proposal within 48 hours.

Thanks —
Vanessa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Vanessa — thanks. Attached is the 7-day export (helio_token_profile.csv). High level:
- Peak concurrent requests: 1,100 RPS (customer-facing web UI, peak window ~10-12 PST)
- Request mix: ~50% <128 tokens, ~30% 128-512, ~15% 512-2048, ~5% >2048
- Streaming/function-calls: ~22% of total (chat sessions that hold connections open)
- Target SLO: p95 < 250ms for short flows (<128 tokens); p95 < 450ms for mid flows; we care about p99 for >2048 (want to avoid >2s).
- Quiet hours: 03:00–07:00 PST (minimal traffic)

We also included two columns for user-perceived tokens (input vs output) and a column with call type. Let us know if you need more telemetry.

—Aditi

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HelioSync dedicated commit — initial ask and data request

Vanessa / Priyom — I pulled the CSV Aditi shared and sketched the math. Key assumptions and quick estimates below; I'll add these into the sizing worksheet (dedicated-sizing-worksheet.xlsx) and upload.

Traffic & token math (7-day sample):
- Peak RPS observed: 1,100 requests/sec; weighted avg tokens/request = 620 tokens (input+output).
- Effective tokens/sec at peak = 1,100 * 620 = ~682k tokens/sec.

Model mapping assumptions (HelioSync mentioned wanting a mix of high-quality and cost variants):
- Primary model target: redwood-llama-70b-fp16 (baseline latency per token: 0.0006s on A100-80GB equivalent with our batching+KV optimizations)
- Quantized alternative: 8-bit quant variant (latency per token +30% reduction in memory footprint, per-token runtime only modestly slower)

GPU tiling and pool recommendations:
- Conservative (95th-tail headroom): assume 1.5x token/sec cushion -> target sustained tokens/sec capacity = ~1.02M tokens/sec.
- With our serving density (approx 120k tokens/sec per A100-80GB-equivalent GPU for baseline model under continuous batching at mixed sequence lengths), we'd need ~8.5 GPUs -> round to 10 GPUs (buffer and autoscale granularity).
- Recommended (80th): 0.9M tokens/sec -> ~7.5 GPUs -> round to 8 GPUs with a 2-GPU burst reserve for peak windows.
- Cost-optimized (quantized + aggressive batching): can achieve ~160k tokens/sec/GPU -> ~6.4 GPUs at 1.02M tokens/sec -> round to 7 GPUs but riskier on tail latency.

Latency tradeoffs and SLO fit:
- Short-flow p95 <250ms: with 8 GPUs and continuous batching tuned for short flows, should meet p95 consistently; tail p99 sensitive to queueing during peak spikes.
- For >2048 token requests (5%): these drive KV cache pressure and increase per-request GPU occupancy; we should route large requests to a small pool of capability-bound instances (2 dedicated GPUs) to prevent head-of-line blocking.

Operational recommendations:
- Canary plan: start with 8 GPUs dedicated, enable autoscale policy to add up to +2 GPUs on sustained 10-minute peaks. Monitor p95/p99 and token queue depth for the first 72 hours.
- Cache & prefix warmup: advise pre-warming KV for the top 50 highest-frequency prompts before go-live window.
- Throttling: implement graceful backpressure for non-critical endpoints (batching window expansion) if queue depth crosses threshold.

Attachments referenced: sizing worksheet draft and a quick-run script for estimating tokens/sec from real-time metrics. I'll push the XLSX and a short slide with the three scenarios to the Drive link. Thoughts?

Karthik
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Aditi — thanks for the profile and for the quick turnaround, and thanks Karthik for the sizing draft. Summary & recommended next steps below so we have a single action list for the HelioSync commit discussion: 

Summary recommendation (single-number commit for procurement discussion):
- Start commit: 8 dedicated GPUs (A100-80GB-equivalent slate), with automatic burst up to +2 GPUs for sustained peak windows. This balances p95/p99 targets and unit economics.
- Separate large-request pool: reserve 2 smaller instances (can be quantized variants or larger-memory nodes) for requests >2048 tokens to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Expected sustained tokens/sec coverage at peak: ~900k–1.02M tokens/sec depending on scenario; this maps to p95 targets for short and mid flows with the recommended config.

Operational runbook items:
1) Pre-launch (we own): finish KV prefix warmup, validate canary traffic at 50% of peak for 24h.
2) Launch day (HelioSync action): provide scheduled traffic window and enable observability webhook to your SRE channel.
3) Post-launch (first 72h): we monitor p95/p99, token queue depth, and GPU utilization; if p95 degrades, increase burst +2 and throttle non-essential flows.

Docs & next artifacts: I've uploaded the sizing worksheet and a short slide with the three scenarios to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bHelioSyncSizing. I'll also open a HubSpot proposal (HS-2026-0913) with the 8-GPU baseline and optional quantized pool add-on. If this looks good, next step is a short procurement checklist and a draft contract with preferred billing cadence.

Can we schedule a 30-minute technical review with your SREs on Monday (13th) at 10:00 PST? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward.
Vanessa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
